jobs.title: Associate Executive Director
jobs.description:
Overview

About Us

The Associate Executive Director
for Brightview will embrace the vision, the mission and the vibrancy of the organization and will help lead a team in creating and maintaining a vibrant and engaging living environment for Brightview residents… and a great place to work for its Associates. This position will support our growing market in Northern New Jersey, covering our communities in Wayne, Warren, Tenafly, Paramus and Randolph New Jersey.

Responsibilities

In this role, you will work in an entrepreneurial environment and will be empowered to assist with leading your community with creativity and independence. You will help the Executive Director oversee day to day business operations to ensure exceptional quality and service, sustained resident satisfaction and associate engagement, operational efficiency, and strong financial results.

As the Associate Executive Director, you’ll be involved in every facet of the operation – Hospitality, Health Services, Dining, Programming, Sales, Maintenance, and the Business Office. You’ll have the opportunity to truly make your mark while making a difference in the lives of both residents and associates.

We will leverage your existing leadership, management, and customer service skills, and in turn we will give you the experience and information you’ll need to be successful in the future as an Executive Director for Brightview in this region.

Supervisory responsibilities will be determined by community but generally consist of the direct oversight of three to five department heads, assisting the Executive Director with the direction of the remaining Department Heads and all other associates as indirect reports. You'll carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with Brightview's policies and procedures and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring and training associates; planning, assigning and directing work; evaluating performance; rewarding and disciplining associates and addressing complaints and resolving problems.

Salary Range

USD $105,000.00 - USD $115,000.00 /Yr.

Compensation Disclosure

The salary range mentioned above reflects the potential pay for this role and does not include bonuses or additional incentives (if applicable), nor does it include the value of our benefit program. Offers will consider factors like experience, qualifications, location, community size (if relevant), certifications/training, etc. Brightview regularly reviews and adjusts compensation ranges.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in related field and/or equivalent experience.
One to three years of management experience in a similar environment.
Proficient in MS Office products, internet and industry specific software programs for marketing, payroll and accounts payable/receivable.
Meet state licensing requirements (where applicable).
Excellent customer service, interpersonal, and communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to lead people and get results through others.
Ability to make independent decisions when circumstances warrant such action.
Ability to prioritize, organize and manage multiple tasks.
Problem analysis and resolution at both strategic and functional levels.
Ability to effectively communicate in English.

Why work at Brightview?

Discover the Brightview Senior Living Difference!

Dedicated to Excellence: We lead the industry with a passion for delivering top-notch services and groundbreaking care.
Embracing Community: Join a supportive and inclusive environment that prioritizes your professional growth, development and advancement.
Impactful Work: Make a meaningful difference in the lives of our seniors, contributing to their joy and well-being every day.
Comprehensive Benefits: Enjoy competitive salaries, health, vision and dental insurance options, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, employee assistance programs and many more benefits that prioritize your well-being.
A Place to Flourish: Embrace diversity, foster innovation, and access the tools and resources for personal and professional growth. Join our vibrant team at Brightview Senior Living and be valued as an integral part of our community.

Equal Opportunity Employer

The State Medical Group Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the senior operational executive responsible for state-wide performance, integration, and optimization of the Medical Group across the state. This leader drives strategic execution, operational excellence, financial stewardship, and cultural alignment in support of the ministry’s mission. The State COO ensures care delivery models are scalable, high-reliability, patient-centered, and aligned with system strategy and state-level regulatory, competitive, and community needs.

Leads the statewide operational strategy for the Medical Group, ensuring alignment with system mission, vision, and strategic plans across acute, ambulatory, and clinically integrated networks.
Develops statewide performance frameworks, playbooks, and operating models that ensure consistency, scalability, and standardization across markets.
Serves as a key advisor to the State CCO, informing long-range planning, market positioning, population health readiness, and network integration

Strengthen dyad leadership structures, ensuring high-performing partnerships that support accountability and engagement.

Partners with state and system leaders to optimize referral stream performance, network leakage reduction, and care coordination across the continuum.

Directs and mentors operational directors, creating succession pipelines and talent development plans across the state.
Serves as a visible statewide ambassador for the ministry, fostering collaboration, trust, and accountability.
Represents the Medical Group at the state executive leadership table, system committees, and community forums.
Strengthens relationships with key stakeholders including physicians, community partners, payers, and government agencies.

Qcells is seeking an accomplished and highly experienced Senior Director, Government Relations to join its Public Policy and Government Relations team. Policy Portfolio Ownership: Develop and execute advocacy strategies for an assigned portfolio of legislative, regulatory, tax, trade, permitting, manufacturing, and energy policy priorities, aligned with direction from the Head of Government Relations.

Strong project management skills and the ability to coordinate senior cross-functional stakeholders, external partners, and parallel workstreams.
Ability to become effective quickly in a fast-paced environment while exercising discretion, adaptability, and exceptional attention to detail.
Executive presence and demonstrated success building trusted relationships with senior government, industry, and corporate stakeholders.

Substantial experience with federal energy, manufacturing, trade, tax, permitting, or infrastructure policy.

Demonstrated success managing complex legislative, regulatory, coalition, or issue advocacy campaigns with measurable business impact.
Deep understanding of clean energy, domestic manufacturing policy, federal tax incentives, and the commercial implications of government action.
Experience serving as a senior subject-matter expert or portfolio owner within a larger government relations function, including mentoring colleagues and

Founded in 1974, Resilience is the only stand-alone rape crisis center in Illinois and has spent more than five decades supporting survivors of sexual violence and advancing systemic change. Formerly known as Rape Victim Advocates, Resilience adopted its current name in 2018 to reflect a broader vision of healing, empowerment, and transformation.

With a $3 million budget, currently there are 34 full and part-time staff, with a number of roles to be filled, and a network of 150 dedicated volunteers, providing free, 24-hour crisis intervention and advocacy services across Chicago-area hospitals. Last year, the organization served more than 1,500 survivors and their loved ones and reached tens of thousands more through public education and professional training.

Resilience is at an important inflection point. Demand for services is growing, new opportunities are emerging, and the organization has ambitious ideas for expanding programs and developing new revenue streams. The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to stabilize and strengthen the organization, build the infrastructure needed for long-term effectiveness, and then lead Resilience into its next phase of thoughtful, sustainable growth.

A critical priority will be financial sustainability. Approximately 72% of Resilience's revenue comes from public dollars distributed through the Illinois Coalition Against Sexual Assault (ICASA). The Executive Director will bring a strong record of fundraising and financial management and lead efforts to diversify revenue through private philanthropy, earned revenue, and other strategic opportunities.

The Executive Director will also strengthen management systems, organizational infrastructure, accountability, and internal communication. Working closely with the Board and staff, they will develop and implement a strategic plan, establish clear priorities, and strengthen alignment between the Board and staff. An important part of the role will be building consensus around Resilience's voice, priorities, and positions.

As the public face of Resilience, successful candidates must be a confident, compelling communicator with the credibility to engage effectively with survivors, staff, volunteers, funders, government leaders, community partners, and the broader public.

The ideal candidate will bring a demonstrated record of nonprofit leadership, fundraising, financial and business management, strategic planning, and organizational development. They will be a collaborative leader who can build trust, navigate complexity, and build consensus around a shared direction and make difficult decisions when necessary.

Demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, anti-oppression, racial justice, and social justice and an understanding of how these principles intersect with survivor services, prevention, organizational culture, and community advocacy is required.

Resilient, adaptable, and effective during change

The Branch Executive Director directs the overall operations of the designated YMCA branch. This position is responsible for implementing the operations strategy to reach the annual strategic and fiscal objectives. Emulates the cause-driven leader on duty practices at all times.

Ensures that the member experience is at the center of everything we do.
Creates a culture of inclusion to ensure the mission of the Y is upheld, diversity is valued, and all are welcome.

Founded in 1974, Resilience is the only stand-alone rape crisis center in Illinois and has spent more than five decades supporting survivors of sexual violence and advancing systemic change. Formerly known as Rape Victim Advocates, Resilience adopted its current name in 2018 to reflect a broader vision of healing, empowerment, and transformation.

With a $3 million budget, currently there are 34 full and part-time staff, with a number of roles to be filled, and a network of 150 dedicated volunteers, providing free, 24-hour crisis intervention and advocacy services across Chicago-area hospitals. Last year, the organization served more than 1,500 survivors and their loved ones and reached tens of thousands more through public education and professional training.

Resilience is at an important inflection point. Demand for services is growing, new opportunities are emerging, and the organization has ambitious ideas for expanding programs and developing new revenue streams. The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to stabilize and strengthen the organization, build the infrastructure needed for long-term effectiveness, and then lead Resilience into its next phase of thoughtful, sustainable growth.

A critical priority will be financial sustainability. Approximately 72% of Resilience's revenue comes from public dollars distributed through the Illinois Coalition Against Sexual Assault (ICASA). The Executive Director will bring a strong record of fundraising and financial management and lead efforts to diversify revenue through private philanthropy, earned revenue, and other strategic opportunities.

The Executive Director will also strengthen management systems, organizational infrastructure, accountability, and internal communication. Working closely with the Board and staff, they will develop and implement a strategic plan, establish clear priorities, and strengthen alignment between the Board and staff. An important part of the role will be building consensus around Resilience's voice, priorities, and positions.

As the public face of Resilience, successful candidates must be a confident, compelling communicator with the credibility to engage effectively with survivors, staff, volunteers, funders, government leaders, community partners, and the broader public.

The ideal candidate will bring a demonstrated record of nonprofit leadership, fundraising, financial and business management, strategic planning, and organizational development. They will be a collaborative leader who can build trust, navigate complexity, and build consensus around a shared direction and make difficult decisions when necessary.

Demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, anti-oppression, racial justice, and social justice and an understanding of how these principles intersect with survivor services, prevention, organizational culture, and community advocacy is required.
